# v0.9.4 - Read It Back: `gc` Proves the New Pack by Content, and a Snapshot Checks Its Payload Objects After the Push

## What's Changed in v0.9.4

The remaining items of the 0.9.3 review round, all of them about trusting what a server says. Checked
on the stub, on Linux (Debian under WSL), and against a real Seafile server (CE 13.0.28, scratch
library): the opt-in real-server tier, a payload snapshot with restore and verify, and a full `gc`
followed by a clone and `fsck`. The suite is 1079 tests.

### Changed

- **`gc` and the tail merge read the new pack back and compare SHA-256 before deleting anything.** The
  listing only proves a size, and a same-length substitution (a padded partial write, a damaged
  block) passed it and led to the originals being deleted. The check costs one more download of the
  new pack under the lock already held, about 0.015 s per MiB.
- **A snapshot run lists its payload objects once more after the push.** A `--payload-delete` on
  another machine can remove an object between the pre-push check and the ref landing. The object is
  uploaded again when the source file is as it was; otherwise the run exits 1 naming it.
- **A ref deletion is read back.** A server that answers 200 without deleting is an error now, not `ok`.

### Tests

- The unreadable-directory guard and the forced English git messages are covered on Windows too (the
  earlier test needed POSIX permissions and was skipped there).

### Not changed, on purpose

- Bounding the server's `Date` offset was rejected: a client clock that is wrong is exactly what the
  offset exists to absorb.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
